title: Multi-value --lora-path/--lora-scale produce a LIST that crashes when fed to scalar pipeline kwargs
detail: The CLI registers --lora-scale/--lora-path as repeated/multi flags (action=append-style), so args.lora_scale / args.lora_path arrive as a Python list. Several command modules pass this list straight into a scalar kwarg: profile hands args.lora_path to pipeline.generate(lora_path=...) (expects one path), faceswap wraps args.lora_scale into lora_scales=[lora_scale] producing a nested list [[...]], expansion assigns the whole list to scalar lora_scale, and workflow stuffs the list into RunConfig.lora_scale (a float dataclass field). All four are latent crashes that only fire when a user actually passes the flag along that code path — static checks miss them. Fix pattern: unwrap to a scalar at the boundary, or make the pipeline kwargs accept lists consistently. Found via effort:low review-only scan (4 of 13 findings).

title: A flag's required=True is NOT satisfied by its --alias when both share the same dest
detail: refine.py registers --input-image with required=True, then app/commands/_shared registers --input to the SAME dest (input_image). argparse only recognizes the original option string for the required check, so a caller using --input (the alias) is rejected as missing-required even though the value landed in the dest. Net effect: the --input alias is permanently unusable for refine. General rule: when aliasing an option via shared dest, set required=True on only ONE registration and never rely on an alias to satisfy a required flag. Found via effort:low review-only scan (2 of 13 findings, one scored high).

title: Frame-floor helpers that early-return on a mod predicate bypass the minimum-frames guarantee
detail: video-vbvr._adjust_frames returns frames=1 unchanged when (frames-1)%8==0 — the modulo predicate is satisfied by 1 (since 0%8==0), so the 9-frame minimum is silently bypassed for that input. Pattern: any floor/ceiling helper whose guard is a divisibility/mod check rather than a direct comparison (frames < MIN) can pass the boundary value straight through. Always express floors as explicit numeric comparisons, not as side-effects of a mod branch. Found via effort:low review-only scan (1 of 13, medium).

title: A ternary expression used as a bare statement discards its value — correctness depends on side-effect ordering
detail: video-relay uses `x if cond else y` as a standalone statement (not assigned). The ternary evaluates only one branch and throws the result away, so any code that relied on BOTH branches' side-effects (e.g. shutil.move ordering) is fragile. Linters rarely flag it because it is syntactically valid. Rewrite as an explicit if/else so the intended branch's side-effect is unambiguous. Found via effort:low review-only scan (1 of 13, low).

title: effort:low review-only scan surfaces genuine latent bugs with ~0 adversarial overturn
detail: Default cheap lane (lanes:[review,lint], fix.mode=review-only) on 2026-06-19T22-02-03 produced 13 findings, ALL 13 passed adversarial verification (upheld=0 overturned). Distribution: high=5, medium=4, low=4; dimensions hit were correctness(6) + argparse-integrity(7) only — type-safety/error-handling/import-hygiene were clean for this scope. Takeaway: the low-effort review lane has a high signal rate; run it routinely and only escalate to medium+fix when you want changes applied. Adversarial-verify on effort:low is near-ceremony here (0/13 overturned) — consider skipping it to cut cost on routine scans.

title: Findings cluster in command modules at the argparse→pipeline boundary (image-*, video-*, refine)
detail: All 13 findings live in app/commands/ modules where argparse args (lists, required flags) meet pipeline dataclasses (scalars) — the type-coercion/dest-collision seam. No findings in app/pipelines, app/workflows, or app/lib. Review focus on app/commands/* yields the highest bug density for this codebase; the boundary between user-facing argparse and typed pipeline constructors is the dominant defect locus. Lint lane (pyflakes/check-model/self-test) was clean this run (pyflakesRealCount=0, selftestOk=true; checkModelOk=false is an infra state, not a code defect).
